Tap the model name to change it (decision 0011).
Flow after a PASS: preview and smoke test, then UAT, then Shipping lands it after your yes (decision 0016).

controls.name: Effort (summary)
controls.what: Repeats the effort selected below, so the one-tap start (number 3) shows everything it will use.
controls.from: The selected effort, number 10.

controls.name: Effort label and ⓘ
controls.what: Names the picker. The ⓘ says: "How hard the models think. More brains is slower and costs more."
controls.from: Fixed text, agreed in design chat 3, turn 77.
notes: Your word is effort, not budget or thinking (decision 0007).

controls.name: Small (one brain)
controls.what: Lowest effort. In pstack's terms the budget "small": every model thinks at medium reasoning.
controls.from: pstack's budget ladder (setup-pstack, step 3). Mastra Code sets effort for the whole session, not per helper (fact F-06).

controls.name: Medium (two brains)
controls.what: pstack's budget "medium": high reasoning.
controls.from: As 8.

controls.name: Large (three brains, selected)
controls.what: pstack's budget "large": extra-high reasoning. Shown selected because it was last time's choice.
controls.from: As 8. Selected state: your last choice.

controls.name: Unlimited (four brains)
controls.what: pstack's budget "unlimited": maximum reasoning.
controls.from: As 8.

controls.name: Building group (open)
controls.what: One row for pstack's four building roles. The model shown applies to all four. The arrow (pointing up) closes the group; here it is open.
controls.from: The group model and each role's model: the pstack model settings (today a file, ~/.agents/pstack-models.md, written by setup-pstack). Whether the dashboard writes that file or keeps its own copy is for the build to decide.
notes: The group names are the advisor's (design chat 3, turn 63); you accepted them. The roles inside are pstack's real names.
Every model shows its real price, ↓$in/$out↑ (decision 0013). The picture shows none here.

controls.name: feature/refactoring
controls.what: pstack role: builds new features, or reorganizes code without changing what it does. Its model is on the right; ⓘ shows that explanation.
controls.from: pstack role line "feature, refactoring". Explanation from pstack's own skill files (design chat 3, turn 71).
notes: Tap the model name to change this one role (decision 0011).

controls.name: bug-fix
controls.what: pstack role: reproduces a reported problem, finds the cause, fixes it.
controls.from: pstack role line "bug-fix".
notes: Tap the model name to change this one role (decision 0011).

controls.name: perf-issue
controls.what: pstack role: fixes one measured slowness.
controls.from: pstack role line "perf-issue".
notes: Tap the model name to change this one role (decision 0011).

controls.name: hillclimb
controls.what: pstack role: keeps improving one number toward a target. Its ⓘ is shown tapped.
controls.from: pstack role line "hillclimb".
notes: Tap the model name to change this one role (decision 0011).

controls.name: Explanation popup
controls.what: What appears when you tap a role's ⓘ: "Keeps improving one number toward a target, trying one idea at a time and keeping only what helps."
controls.from: Fixed text per role, from pstack's skill files.
notes: Explanations show only when the ⓘ is tapped (C-09).

controls.name: Judgment group
controls.what: Two roles: judgment and prose (writing and judgment calls); hardest tasks (the trickiest code changes). Group model GPT-6 Sol. Arrow opens it.
controls.from: pstack role lines "judgment and prose", "hardest tasks".
notes: The picture's "$$$$" is replaced by real prices, ↓$in/$out↑ (decision 0013).

controls.name: Investigating group
controls.what: Four roles: how explorer (reads the code to find how something works), how explainer (turns that into a plain explanation), why investigators (dig through history for why something was built this way), why synthesizer (pulls the findings into one answer with sources).
controls.from: pstack role lines "how explorer", "how explainer", "why investigators", "why synthesizer".

controls.name: Learning group
controls.what: Two roles: reflect tooling (reviews a finished session for lessons about tools); reflect judgment (for lessons about decisions). Group model Beam, shown Free because it costs nothing right now.
controls.from: pstack role lines "reflect tooling", "reflect judgment, divergent, synthesizer". Free comes from the current price: Beam is free only for a limited-time promotion.

controls.name: Panels group
controls.what: Four roles that each run several models side by side: arena runners (several models attempt the same task), arena cross-judge pool (models that may judge those attempts), architect runners (several models sketch the design before code), interrogate reviewers (models that try to break the change). Each holds a list of models; one helper runs per model, so the list's length sets how many run.
controls.from: pstack role lines for the four panels; list rule from setup-pstack step 3.
notes: With the group open, each panel's models are chips with ×, plus "+ Add"; at least one stays (decision 0012).

controls.name: Workers group
controls.what: One role: swarm workers (parallel helpers for many small jobs and for checking work).
controls.from: pstack role line "swarm workers".

controls.name: Finish ping
controls.what: Tells you that when the build finishes, you get a Linear notification. It is a line of information, not a switch.
controls.from: Today: Mastra Code's "agent done" notification runs the stop-ping script, which comments on the card and sets you a Linear reminder (decision record 0024). For builds started from the dashboard the same must happen.

controls.name: Start
controls.what: Starts the build with the settings as they are on screen now, after any changes. Fixed to the bottom so it is always in reach.
controls.from: The choices on this screen. Starting a build: created by the build (decision 0009).
notes: Number 3 starts with last time's settings untouched; number 24 starts with what you changed here.
